Three declaration positions for that local were probed (before result / after result / after range); positions 1 and 3 were strictly worse and positions 2 and the untested-4th measured IDENTICAL results, so the declaration-position axis is dead by the two-identical-A/B rule. NEXT AGENT: this is the lane's closest exact -- attack the register numbering (ours r30/r6, target r29/r9) or the entry schedule, not the declaration order. show_gold 89.3784% -> 89.4459%, real 127 -> 117; residual target-only +3 add, the rematerialise-vs-cache of `base + col*12` across four pile pointers, unchanged by every variant tried. do_shopping_8009AA48 92.2517% -> 92.3667%, real 831 -> 826, insns T870/O866; the gain came ONLY from the extern retype reaching its base local, not from any member respelling. fn_8009A0AC byte-identical (real 187, T154/O153): four raw-offset pile blocks converted to named members with zero score movement; its own residual is target-only +3 add (same rematerialise class) plus an ours-only srawi+slwi in the seeds loop, on which two source forms measured IDENTICALLY negative (194, 194) and killed that axis. write_shop_menu NO CHANGE RETAINED: two full conversions (whole-population, and around-the-protected-webs) each improved the opcode multiset (16 -> 13 and 16 -> 12 tokens) and instruction-count parity (393 -> 394/395 against 401) while REGRESSING fuzzy 90.2968% -> 89.3491% / 89.1596% and real 374 -> 391/402; both reverted on the monotonic rule. do_shop SCREENED, NOT CONVERTED: baseline real 614, T459/O453, multiset 20t, target-only +8 add +4 lwz +1 stwx. It has four isolated `add`+`lwz` vs our `addi`+`lwzx` sites that are exactly the show_piles shape -- @0x46c reads blits[x][4] (page + pl*24 + 7520), @0x490 reads item_blits[player][j] (page + player*256 + 6480 + j*4), @0x5d4 and @0x280 similar, the last being a stride-60 PadStateView read that is NOT the shop buffer. It was left unconverted deliberately: it is the most scattered population in the TU (five stride groups plus five `oNN` byte-offset accumulator webs) and the new law predicts a net loss there.
